title: Davide Derocchi
description: Case notes on the Davide Derocchi site — a virtualized contact-sheet wall, silent motion tiles and a footer that doubles as an invoice line
summary: Photographer portfolio with masked view transitions and per-route subsetted variable fonts
notes: The site is one continuous contact-sheet wall — every still and motion frame from Paris, Milan and New York laid on a light-table grid, virtualized into one absolutely-positioned layer so 400-plus plates scroll without a dropped frame
Row rhythm follows his print contact sheets — 4px gutters, mixed plate ratios snapped to a 12-column masonry and every row landing flush, so the wall reads as one plane at any width
Motion enters the wall as silent looping tiles — poster frame first, decoder attached only inside a 300px viewport margin and dropped again on exit, so an idle page never holds more than four streams

items: stills as 300dpi masters with the grade baked in
motion selects as ProRes with poster frames already cut
caption spec naming city, client and season per series

notes: Mobile turns the wall into one full-bleed column on the same 4px rhythm — native momentum only, no scroll hijacking, and the name line pins to the bottom edge as plain type
The footer doubles as the invoice line — DDSTUDIO SRLS details, VAT number and contacts render from the same structured data his billing template reads
He sends new selects straight into the CMS and the wall re-sequences by shoot date — the relationship runs on two catch-up calls a season and zero design escalations
